chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sukkari narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated from al-Jariri, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumamah, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) heard a man say to another: 'May Allah make ugly your face and the face of one who resembles you.' So He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Wait, do not say this, for indeed Allah created Adam in His image.'

The compiler of this book, may Allah have mercy on him, said: I left the anthropomorphists from the beginning of this hadith, and they said: 'Indeed Allah created Adam in His image.' Thus, they went astray in its meaning and led others astray.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of 'Allah created Adam in His image' in Shia theology regarding divine attributes?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Tawhid, the Prophet (SAWW) corrects a man's curse by reminding him that Allah created Adam in His 'image' (Surah), establishing the basis for human dignity. Shaykh al-Saduq notes that while the anthropomorphists (al-Mushabbihah) misinterpreted this phrase to imply a physical form for Allah, the Shia scholarly tradition understands it as a metaphorical reference to attributes or form, preserving divine transcendence (Tanzih).
